To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the effect of stimulus compounding on operant behavior is a function of the associative history of the stimuli involved in the compound.
the summation of stimulus control is not observed when reinforcement is absent during one of the stimuli and is observed when reinforcement is present during both stimuli.

the effect of reinforcement on the distribution of responses is dependent upon the reinforcement associated with the stimuli, and that the effect of a stimulus on response distribution is dependent upon the stimulus associated with reinforcement.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of reinforcement differences on the choice and distribution of responses during stimulus compounding.
the effects on choice and distribution of response that occur when a stimulus is associated with a change in the reinforcement schedule.
stimulus-reinforcer and stimulus-response associations and with the effects of reinforcement differences on the choice of response alternatives.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

additive summation of stimulus control is observed when the stimuli are associated with both response increase and reinforcement increase, but not when the stimulus-reinforcement and stimulus-response associations are in conflict.
the effect of stimulus compounding is a function of the stimulus-receptor, stimulus-response, and stimulus-reinforcement associations conditioned to the individual components of the compound.
additive summation occurs only when stimulus-response and reinforcement associations are both positive.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

stimulus compounding produces additive effects when the stimuli are associated with both response facilitation and reinforcement, and produces additive effects when they are both associated with response facilitation, but not when one stimulus is associated with response increase while the other is associated with reinforcement decrease.
stimulus compounding is not a simple additive summation of individual stimuli.
the effect of stimulus compounding is a function of stimulus-reinforcer contingencies, and that the locus of responding in a multiple or chain schedule is a function of reinforcement-associated cues.
The main takeaway from our work is that

stimulus compounding is an important phenomenon that can be studied in a variety of ways and that the results of these studies can inform our understanding of how stimuli influence behavior in complex environments.
the effect of stimulus compounding depends on the nature of the stimulus-response and stimulus reinforcement associations conditioned to the individual components of the compound.
the effect of compounding two stimuli on choice depends on their associative history.
